s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion
salient_findings: 3-month history of progressive swelling in the right upper posterior tooth region
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Ground-glass trabecular pattern with radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars on radiographs
key_facts: 9-year-old boy presented with a painless swelling
Swelling located in the right upper posterior tooth region
Swelling had grown progressively over 3 months
Facial asymmetry present
Medical and family histories were unremarkable
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Overlying skin was normal
Intraorally, a 4.0×3.0 cm ovoid, hard, nontender swelling in the right buccal vestibule
Buccal cortical expansion and slight palatal expansion present
No mucosal changes
Radiographs showed a ground-glass trabecular pattern
Radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars
Cone-beam CT revealed expansion of the buccal and palatal cortical plates
Involvement of more than half of the right maxillary sinus

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical and radiological findings of a well-defined, hard, nontender swelling with a ground-glass trabecular pattern and buccal cortical expansion

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a ground-glass appearance, but less likely due to the well-defined margin of the swelling

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion, although typically bilateral

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of a hard, nontender swelling with radiolucency around the roots of teeth

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to juvenile ossifying fibroma, with a possible diagnosis given the clinical and radiological findings

shortlist.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that includes juvenile ossifying fibroma and fibrous dysplasia, with a possible diagnosis given the clinical and radiological findings

shortlist.label: Odontogenic myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely, but possible diagnosis given the presence of a hard, nontender swelling with buccal cortical expansion

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely, but possible diagnosis given the presence of a hard, nontender swelling with radiolucency around the roots of teeth

raw.rationale: The well-defined margin of the swelling and the ground-glass internal pattern on radiographs are characteristic of juvenile ossifying fibroma, distinguishing it from fibrous dysplasia which typically has an ill-defined margin.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Ill-defined margin and merging with surrounding areas are typical of fibrous dysplasia, which contradicts the well-defined margin observed in this case

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Typically presents with bilateral involvement of the mandible and maxilla, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Often has a more aggressive radiographic appearance and may be associated with root resorption, not mentioned in this case

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Similar to juvenile ossifying fibroma but typically has a more mixed radiolucent and radiopaque appearance

rejected.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: A broader category that includes juvenile ossifying fibroma, but the specific characteristics of this case point more directly to juvenile ossifying fibroma

rejected.label: Odontogenic myxoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more radiolucent appearance and may be associated with tooth displacement, not described in this case

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Usually associated with systemic symptoms of hyperparathyroidism and multiple bone lesions, not indicated in this case
